Water was good. It supported Life. It healed. And there were yet to be any sentient beings on Ebos within its freshwater streams or crystal clear lakes.

Pomme was tired from birth, but she wanted more creations, so impressed she was with Silvano and inspired by the living stone of Carraig. She wished for the water itself to live. She wanted it to learn, to mimic, to emulate the sentient life living around it, drinking from it, swimming through it.

The powerful being she had hoped to create was different than her plan, but such is the chaos of nature. As she observed her creations she realized that they were inherently good, but also petty, and easily offended. [Taking the form of whichever Avatar it was in which she spoke to them](https://i.sli.mg/MvWU02.jpg), she noted that it was now two creations in a row which changed shape at a whim.

If she flattered them or spoke nicely to them as one would speak to a child, they, in turn, responded favorably to her. Once a water form was so smitten with her that it dragged her Avatar to the depths of the lake from which they met, showing her all of the interesting things that had accumulated. This one instance made her worry for the safety of mortals who required breath.

During the course of her observations, they healed fully a Tanngrisnir that had limped to the rivers edge after an attack by some Zefflins. The water had taken the form of other Tannsgrisnirs and tended to its wounds until it was able to walk back to its herd.

She was never sure if it was many creatures, or one which was capable of taking many forms, sentient and shy, or only able to mimic. She intended them to be a sentient species, they seemed as immortal and dynamic as the rivers. Many had appeared to her at once, and sometimes only one, mimicking her movements exactly. Their lives seemed endless, for they lived in and from and *were* the moving waters of Ebos.
